sources.document: Características Geodinámicas en el Distrito de Paita (Provincia de Paita - Región Piura), Informe Técnico N°032-2021/IGP
admissible_claims: IGP identifies the named ravines Nueva Esperanza, La Piscina, Catarata and Villa Naval in Paita.
IGP states that waters from those named ravines finally flow through the main ravine called El Zanjón.
IGP states that the El Zanjón system ultimately discharges toward the Pacific Ocean.
IGP field documentation reports an activation context for Quebrada Catarata with mudflow impacts, without a date that can be used as a child-level dated event.
IGP documents local ravine and pluvial processes in Paita separately from lower-Chira river flooding.
forbidden_inferences: PDF figure linework is not reproducible GIS geometry and must not be digitized as exact channel, catchment or outlet geometry.
The static tributary-to-El-Zanjón relation does not locate exact confluences or provide travel times, attenuation, discharge or hydraulic routing.
General statements about activation during rainy or El Niño periods are not dated child-level event labels.
The Quebrada Catarata field activation context may not be assigned an event date absent a dated primary record.
Statements about saturation or overflow do not establish a numerical hydraulic capacity for El Zanjón.
Historical rainfall context cited by the report is not automatically event-paired to an individual Paita ravine and cannot define an IRFEN threshold.
No observation or impact from the Río Chira or Colán may be transferred to the Paita urban ravines.
No risk class, threshold, probability or operational alert may be inferred from this report.
